items.name: Mistral Large 4 open weights (Le Chonk)
items.summary: Mistral released the open weights of its improved 1-trillion-parameter flagship on October 29, three weeks after its October 6 preview. The natively multimodal mixture-of-experts model (52 billion active parameters, 1-million-token context) leads open-weight coding benchmarks including FrontierCode 2.0 (19.7%) and can now be self-hosted under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight Licence.

items.name: GitHub Copilot Fusion
items.summary: GitHub made Copilot Fusion generally available on October 28: instead of picking a model per task, developers choose an effort level (Standard, High or Max) and Copilot routes and orchestrates models for each task. GitHub says Fusion Max scored 60 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, near Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max, at about half the API cost per task.

items.name: Liquid AI LFM3
items.summary: Liquid AI announced LFM3 on October 27, a family of six open-weight models of around 2 billion parameters — text, vision, audio, omni and two decision models — all branched from one shared backbone trained on 22 trillion tokens. Built for on-device agents, the 1.7B text model fits in about 1 GB of memory at 4-bit precision with a 256K-token context window.

items.name: Baseten joey-1
items.summary: Baseten released joey-1 on October 29, a 2B-parameter open-weight decision model that returns a calibrated label and confidence score instead of generated text, for high-volume routing, classification and guardrail checks. Post-trained from Qwen3.5-2B, it costs $0.01 per million tokens with a reported 20 ms P50 latency, and its weights are on Hugging Face under the MIT licence.
